status.title: Status
status.name: Name
status.enabled_domains: No domains enabled | {n} domain enabled | {n} domains enabled

domains.title: Domains
domains.intro: Enable email client autoconfiguration for one or more of your mail domains. Newly discovered domains are disabled by default.
domains.no_domains_description: No domains were found on the configured mail instance.
domains.updating: Updating… this can take up to a minute
domains.dnshelper_absent_description: DNS records for enabled domains must be created manually. Install ns8-dnshelper to manage them from here.
domains.waiting_for_dns_description: The route for {domain} hasn't been set up yet because its DNS records don't resolve to this node. It will be created automatically once they do -- open the DNS status dialog to see what's needed, or to check again.
domains.route_failure_description: The Traefik route for {domain} could not be created. Check the module's logs for details.

dns_status.title: DNS status for {domain}
dns_status.manual_title: DNS is not managed by dnshelper for this domain
dns_status.manual_description: Create the records below with your DNS provider, then check again.
dns_status.not_permitted_title: dnshelper has no access rule for this zone
dns_status.not_permitted_description: dnshelper manages the zone {zone}, but this module has no rule to change it. Ask an administrator to add one in dnshelper's Access page.
dns_status.partly_permitted_title: dnshelper's access rule does not cover every record
dns_status.partly_permitted_description: This module has a rule for the zone {zone}, but it does not cover the records marked "Not permitted", so this module can neither see nor change them. Ask an administrator to extend the rule in dnshelper's Access page.

profile_link.title: Profile link for {domain}
profile_link.intro: Share this with your users so they can download their mail client configuration, or embed the snippet below on a page you control.
profile_link.snippet_description: A self-contained form, no external JS or CSS. Paste it as-is into a page you control.
profile_link.no_auth_description: This link and form are unauthenticated by design, like the autoconfiguration protocols themselves: anyone who knows an address can request its mail settings.

domain_settings.title: Settings for {domain}
domain_settings.intro: Choose what clients asking about this domain receive. A setting left at Default follows the Settings page, and changes with it.

settings.title: Settings
settings.mail_server_help: The mail server whose domains this instance configures clients for. If you change it, domains only the previous one has stop being served and show as orphaned on the Domains page.
settings.mail_server_missing_description: The mail server this instance is bound to is no longer on the cluster, so nothing is being served. Choose another one and save.
settings.service_host_help: CNAME/SRV target and Autodiscover host. Leave blank to use this node's own FQDN.
settings.display_names_tooltip: Looked up from LDAP for the address a client asks about.
settings.resolve_aliases_tooltip: For an alias that delivers to one user, give out that user's login. Aliases shared by several users are not resolved.
settings.display_names_notice_description: Autoconfiguration endpoints answer any request, without a password. With display names on, a display name is included for whichever address is asked about, along with the mail server names; with alias resolution on, the login behind an alias is included too. Turn them off to reduce what an anonymous request reveals, at the cost of clients showing the raw address instead of a name, or asking users of an alias to type their login.
settings.domain_defaults_description: Display names, alias resolution and the calendar, contacts and ActiveSync providers apply to every domain, unless a domain overrides them under Domain settings on the Domains page.
settings.groupware_description: Also publish the CalDAV/CardDAV or ActiveSync endpoint of a groupware app, so clients set those up along with mail. Users log in with the same user name as for mail.
settings.groupware_none_found_description: Nextcloud, SOGo or WebTop can be offered here once installed, configured with a host name, and bound to the same user domain as the mail server. ActiveSync also requires SOGo or WebTop to use this mail server. Nextcloud must run on this node.
settings.sign_profiles_tooltip: Signs downloaded .mobileconfig profiles with the certificate of the service host, so Apple devices show them as verified. This puts that certificate's private key in the automx container.
settings.signing_ok_description: Apple profiles are signed with the certificate of {host}.
settings.signing_untrusted_description: Profiles are signed with the certificate of {host}, but this server does not trust that certificate, so devices will probably show the profile as unverified.
settings.signing_problem_no_certificate: There is no certificate for {host} yet. Profiles will be signed once there is one, either issued by Let's Encrypt or uploaded in the certificate settings.
settings.signing_problem_not_available: The certificate of {host} could not be read. See the logs for details.
settings.signing_problem_unreadable: The certificate or key of {host} could not be read.
settings.signing_problem_not_rsa: The certificate of {host} does not use an RSA key, which profile signing requires.
settings.signing_problem_key_too_small: The key of the certificate of {host} is shorter than 2048 bits.
settings.signing_problem_key_mismatch: The certificate of {host} does not match its key.
settings.signing_problem_expired: The certificate of {host} is expired or not yet valid.
settings.signing_problem_no_digital_signature: The certificate of {host} does not allow digital signatures.

dns_error.domain_not_found: Not a domain of the configured mail instance
dns_error.zone_unmanaged: dnshelper does not manage this domain's zone
dns_error.zone_not_permitted: dnshelper has no access rule for this zone
dns_error.auth_failed: Authentication with the DNS provider failed
dns_error.unsupported: Not supported by this DNS provider
dns_error.groupware_not_available: That app does not provide this service for the mail server.
dns_error.mail_server_not_found: That mail server is not on the cluster.
dns_error.mail_server_in_use: Another automx instance already uses that mail server. Two instances on one mail server would overwrite each other's DNS records.
dns_error.mail_server_not_configured: That mail server is not configured yet. Configure it first.
